reading: Allen 626170538 is a perisomatic fit: all active conductances are somatic and the 60 um axon stub, dendrites and apical tree are passive (dendritic capacitance already spine-scaled to 2.3 uF/cm2, so the load arm ran at 4.6). The soma therefore initiates its own spike by construction. The human upstroke's shoulder (100 to 250 V/s near -45 mV before a 351 V/s main rise to +36 mV) is what a soma shows when the spike arrives from an initiation site through the axial path; a somatic-initiation model must reach the same peak with its own sodium and does so two to three times faster. Stage X showed the two in-family levers (somatic sodium, passive load) each break another row (peak, trough) when they move the rise rate. The Steep X for the E cell lies outside the model family.
mechanism: dV/dt at the soma equals (I_Na,soma - I_axial - I_K - I_leak + I_applied) / C_soma. With no active axon, I_Na,soma must supply both the rise and the peak; in the human the axial term is a source during the shoulder (current from the initiation site), and the somatic sodium activates from a higher voltage with a smaller share of the rise. The rate is bounded by the axial resistance and the soma's load, not by the somatic sodium density.
returned_question: Whether to change the E model family by giving the axon an initiation site (insert transient sodium in the stub, or replace the stub with an initial-segment geometry). This is a family change under the fail rule, so it is the user's decision; a first test costs two evaluations (axonal NaTs at 1x and 3x the somatic density, somatic sodium reduced to hold the peak) at about 15 minutes each.
